findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 27:11 David leaves none alive, thinking they would tell of him: the thought of a report drives the killing. In Ecc 9:10 there is no thought in Sheol, to which all are going: thought belongs to life. In Mat 18:12 leaving the ninety-nine is in the case the hearers are asked to think about.
findings.grounds: no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 18:25 Saul says the king desires only a bride-price of foreskins, while he thinks to make David fall by the Philistines: the stated desire covers the thought. In 1Ch 28:9 Solomon is to serve with a willing mind, for the Lord understands every plan and thought. In 2Sa 14:17 and 2Ki 7:12 will is the future of the quoted thought.
findings.grounds: serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind

findings.obs_text: In Psa 56:5 and Isa 59:7 the thoughts are of evil, with injury, desolation and destruction around them: the thoughts lead to harm. In Isa 10:7 the Assyrian's heart thinks to destroy. In 2Cor 10:5 the destroying is of arguments, and the thoughts are taken captive.
findings.grounds: it is in his heart to destroy

older.finding: The one who carries it out: "Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger … but it is in his heart to destroy"; "you showed them no mercy"; "while I was angry but a little, they furthered the disaster"; "you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven"; Saul judged for not carrying it out.

findings.obs_text: Death is what the thought fears or expects in Gen 26:9 (Isaac thought he would die because of Rebekah), 1Sa 20:3 (a step between David and death), Job 29:18 (Job thought he would die in his nest) and Jon 1:6 (the captain hopes they will not perish). In Joh 11:13 they took Jesus' word of death for sleep, in Act 8:20 Simon's silver is to perish for his thought, and in 1Cor 4:9 Paul thinks the apostles are like men sentenced to death. In Judg 13:7 death goes with conceive in its bodily sense.
findings.grounds: I shall die in my nest
